response.internal_assessment: Optimizing L2 PARTICIPATE. My role security is the live threat. David is formalizing underwriting criteria and sharing delinquency data with Maria's task force — that is institutional repositioning happening above me, and I need to be visibly aligned with it, not caught flat-footed. The word of mouth confirms David is scheduling a formal 30-minute sit-down with me. That meeting is my most important event this month. Savings are bleeding roughly $1,100 per month — I have ~7 months of runway, which is enough to stay deliberate rather than panicked. The NMLS pathway is active and real, but it is 10 months out. Between now and then I have to be the loan officer David is glad he kept. I show up to that meeting with something: my own read on early delinquencies I've seen cross my desk, my NMLS module progress, and a question about the new underwriting criteria he's formalizing so I can front-run the policy shift in my own processing. I am not asking for reassurance. I am demonstrating that I am already operating in the new reality.

chosen_actions.description: Prepare a written one-page brief for David Chen's formal 30-minute check-in: document the early delinquency patterns I have observed firsthand on auto loans processed in the last 60 days, note the 18% application volume decline I am seeing on the front end, and confirm NMLS module completion progress (modules 1-3 complete, modules 4-6 on schedule). Bring this brief to the meeting as a tangible deliverable — not a presentation, just one page showing I have been paying attention to the same data David is sharing upward. Ask David directly what the new written underwriting criteria will look like and request a draft copy so I can align my intake workflow before it is formally published.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Two to three hours of preparation time. No financial cost. Emotional investment in being seen as a forward-leaning asset rather than a dependent position to manage.
chosen_actions.reasoning: David scheduled this meeting. He is not doing it to fire me — he is doing it because the bank's stress response requires him to know where his people stand. The best thing I can do is arrive with data he does not already have: my ground-level read on delinquency patterns and application drop-off. That positions me as an intelligence source, not a cost center. It also closes the loop on the tick 4 commitment — I told him I was ready to engage, now I show what engagement looks like.

chosen_actions.description: Complete NMLS Modules 4 and 5 this month during the established 90-minute daily blocks. Module 4 covers mortgage loan origination disclosures and timing requirements. Module 5 covers borrower eligibility and income documentation standards. Log completion dates and forward confirmation to David after the meeting so the institutional record reflects continuous progress, not a single burst at the beginning.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Existing 90-minute daily calendar blocks — no new time allocation required. Tuition reimbursement framework already confirmed through HR. Mental bandwidth that previously went toward worrying about the auto loan pipeline redirected toward skill acquisition.
chosen_actions.reasoning: The NMLS pathway is a 10-month runway, but I am one month in. If I let the training slip now — when applications are slow and I have more mental space, not less — I will not recover the schedule when the bank needs to move me. The training is also the most visible proof that the tick 4 commitment was real and not performative. David does not need to ask whether I am still on track if I send him a module completion log every 30 days.

response.inner_monologue: David is building the case upward and I need to make sure that when Sandra or whoever asks who is solid in the auto lending group, my name comes out of his mouth without hesitation.
